mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE falls below 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals increased economic activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of instances where HOUST increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals increased economic output, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO MoM growth exceeds 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals robust economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances where both RSAFS and PAYEMS increase.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% YoY, it signals a restrictive monetary policy in a low-growth environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2% and GDPC1 YoY growth < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS MoM growth > 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% MoM signals deflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL MoM decline exceeds 0.5%.
